sources.name: USGS National Transportation Dataset — Trails
sources.query: (name IS NOT NULL AND name <> '') OR hikerpedestrian = 'Y'

sources.name: U.S. Forest Service — National Forest System Trails (land trails open to hikers)
sources.query: trail_type='TERRA' AND trail_name IS NOT NULL AND (allowed_terra_use LIKE '%1%' OR hiker_pedestrian_managed IS NOT NULL OR hiker_pedestrian_accpt IS NOT NULL)

sources.name: Bureau of Land Management — Ground Transportation Linear Features (trails managed for non-motorized public use)
National Park Service — Public Trails (existing, official trails; mountain trails ≥0.3 mi not already listed)
sources.query: TRLNAME IS NOT NULL AND TRLNAME <> ' ' AND TRLNAME <> '' AND TRLSTATUS IN ('Existing','Exisiting','Temporarily Closed') AND (ISEXTANT IS NULL OR ISEXTANT <> 'False') AND (TRLFEATTYPE IS NULL OR TRLFEATTYPE NOT IN ('Unofficial Trail','Unmaintained Trail','Unmaintained Trail Centerline')) AND (TRLTYPE IS NULL OR TRLTYPE NOT IN ('Sidewalk','Water Trail','Snow Trail','Ferry Route'))

sources.name: OpenSkiMap — ski runs (used to identify ski runs; not listed as trails)
sources.query: U.S./Canadian pistes; a record is a run when ≥60% of its line follows a piste

sources.name: OpenStreetMap — trailheads (start points)
sources.query: highway=trailhead within 800 m of a trail end; 17,668 trails matched; OSM data as of 2026-05-06T03:25:00Z

sources.query: route relations in Geofabrik extracts of every U.S. state and Canadian province/territory

sources.query: highway=path|footway|track|bridleway|cycleway with a name, after verification rules R1–R10

notes: Each record is a whole named trail: 495,241 source sections were merged where sections with the same name connect (within 200 m). Same-named trails that do not connect stay separate, except named through-hikes (Appalachian, Pacific Crest, …), which are one trail even across mapping gaps. Unnamed sections are never merged.

Trail length is the sum of its sections with overlapping stretches counted once. U.S. sections use USGS-reported miles when they agree with the mapped line (within 0.67–1.5×); otherwise, and for all Canadian sections, length is measured from the generalized geometry.
Generalized source geometry is for discovery, not navigation. Map pins are points on the trail's longest mapped line, not verified trailheads.
State/province is inferred from the map pin and Natural Earth public-domain boundaries; long trails can extend outside it.
Seasonal access, overnight camping, water, difficulty and elevation are not inferred. Source data may be older than the retrieval date.
U.S. eligibility is named USGS sections plus unnamed sections tagged hikerpedestrian=Y; unnamed sections are labeled Unnamed trail.
Standalone trails shorter than 0.05 mi are mapping fragments and are excluded.

Pieces that the Forest Service records as one official trail (same TRAIL_CN) are joined into it even across mapping gaps; old links redirect. Official agency trails come from the NPS Public Trails layer (existing, official, open or temporarily closed; not unofficial, unmaintained, sidewalk, water or snow trails), U.S. Forest Service National Forest System Trails (land trails where hiking is an allowed use or has a managed season) and BLM transportation data (routes managed for non-motorized or non-mechanized public use). A line already in the catalog within 25 m for ≥60% of its length confirms that trail and is recorded as a source; only new lines become trails. Catalog lines on Forest Service trails that do not allow hiking are rejected. Trails only an agency maps show a sampled elevation range (Copernicus DEM via Open-Meteo).

Every trail is checked by config/trail-quality.json rules: 94,484 passed, 20,775 are short trails, 3,903 need review and 27,296 are partial, unnamed or connector segments kept out of default results. No elevation is available from these sources.
1,527 records follow downhill ski pistes mapped in OpenSkiMap and are listed as ski runs, not hiking trails; 2,350 follow Nordic ski tracks and stay hikeable.
Second winter pass: 2998 more records are ski or over-snow routes (lift lines and courses on pistes, U.S. Forest Service snow-only trails, winter-only names) and are listed under Ski, not hiking.

Allowed uses (hiking, biking, horses, snowshoe, cross-country ski, motorized) come from the official use fields of the USGS National Digital Trails sections and the U.S. Forest Service and BLM records; a use is listed when sections allowing it make up at least half the trail. 47,427 trails have official uses; the rest are sorted by name and surface. Trails USGS records as closed to hikers, or open only to motor vehicles, are kept out of foot sections.
Tiers: 144,754 verified (official agency record or OpenStreetMap route relation) and 204,609 mapped (named OpenStreetMap ways that passed every verification rule). Nothing below "mapped" is shown.
Catalog v3: sources are matched by name and geometry (≥50% of a line within 100 m) and merged into one record listing every contributor; old links redirect.

Difficulty: Effort = miles + 2 × (feet of climb ÷ 1,000), so 1,000 ft of climbing counts like 2 flat miles. Easy under 4, Moderate 4–9, Hard 9–16, Very hard 16 and over. The OpenStreetMap sac_scale tag sets a minimum: mountain_hiking is at least Moderate, demanding_mountain_hiking at least Hard, alpine_hiking or harder Very hard. Without a measured climb, distance alone is used.

Quality score: Verified tier +15, OSM relation +25, official source +20, Wikidata +15 (+10 with a Wikipedia article), trailhead +8, named +10, over 1 mi +8, national network +15, regional +8, local +3, inside a park or forest +10; climbers' approach/descent −25, unnamed or fragment −30, under 0.25 mi −10, mapped trail that barely passed the filter −10.

Worldwide: 869,547 trails in 232 countries outside the U.S. and Canada (and in Alaska and Hawaii) from OpenStreetMap — 371,534 route relations and 498,013 named trails — built with the same verification rules.
Pieces together: 19,588 named trails that map data splits into pieces were joined (23,496 pieces, ends within 400 m, same name and activity); gaps between pieces are not drawn or counted.
